description: Test files that exist in this repository and are NOT executed by the pull-request gate. Every entry is a hole in what a green pull request means, stated so that a reader of that green knows what it does not cover. `unrun` — the BROWSER register, whose every field and whose job-summary rendering are about an authenticated spec — is EMPTY at this head, and that is a statement about THAT tier rather than an omission: the tier it used to declare is now executed and governed, and the `governed` block below records what closed it, so the file goes on being the place a reader looks. THE EMPTINESS WAS PHRASED AS THOUGH IT WERE A STATEMENT ABOUT THE WHOLE REPOSITORY, AND IT NEVER WAS ONE. `tests/db/p1-31-export-fixture.test.ts` is executed by no hosted job and by no local aggregate, deliberately: it installs privileged, expiring grants and refuses to run against the shared acceptance database, so it needs a disposable one that no runner has. A green pull request therefore does not cover it, which is exactly the kind of hole this file exists to name, and while the file said nothing about it the silence read as an absence. It is declared in `unrunNonBrowser`, which is a SECOND register and not a widening of the first: admitting a database path to `unrun` would have meant relaxing the inversion guard in tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts that refuses any declaration outside the gated browser directory, and that guard is the only reason a declaration cannot be used to excuse a tier the gate really runs. Both registers are held to their own required fields by that same file.
whyThisFileExists: apps/web/playwright.config.ts gates tests/e2e/authenticated/** behind ROOTLCO_E2E_AUTH === '1'. For the whole of P1-27 no workflow set it, so the repository's ONLY end-to-end tenant-isolation proof and its ONLY route-level accessibility proof had never once executed anywhere but on the Owner's machine, while `test:web-e2e` reported a green browser tier and the phase records counted browser coverage. Nothing said so anywhere. This file, the LOUD job-summary step in .github/workflows/_reusable-node-quality.yml that reads it, and tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts are what replaced that silence.
whatChangedAndWhatDidNot: TWO changes, a phase apart. FIRST the tier was WIRED: a job stood the Supabase stack up with the vendored CLI, bootstrapped the real operator and the second tenant through scripts/dev/owner-acceptance/create-owner-account.mjs, started the production API build as a database login holding neither SUPERUSER nor BYPASSRLS, ran `npm run test:web-e2e-authenticated` with ROOTLCO_E2E_AUTH=1, and FAILED unless every authenticated spec file contributed at least one executed test. The earlier claim recorded here — that a hosted runner cannot be given a live Supabase, a live API and a real account — was false: a hosted runner has Docker and the Supabase CLI is a devDependency of this repository. SECOND, and this is what emptied `unrun`, the tier became GOVERNED: the job body moved to .github/workflows/_reusable-authenticated-browser.yml, both `pr-ci.yml` and `protected-develop-verification.yml` call it, `authenticated-browser` is in DECLARED_JOBS in scripts/ci/evaluate-ci-gate.mjs, and it is in the `needs` of both `ci-gate` and `protected-gate`. Neither gate can report Go while this check is red. What did NOT change is the strength of the tier itself: the same specs, the same zero-test guard.
hostedObservation: OBSERVED SIX TIMES, and the last three PASSED. Recorded run by run, because a single sentence about this tier has already been wrong twice in this phase — first claiming a hosted runner could not stand the stack up, then claiming the tier had never executed. Both were checked against the GitHub API rather than against this file, which is how they were caught. (1) Run 31337158296, workflow_dispatch on remediation/p1-27-final-canonical-blockers, commit 155a5f55fdd5b6262ea2ed9c421dcf98f5bc83a7, job 93304793606: FAILED. supabase start, supabase:reset across every migration and seed, the identity-provider settings, /auth/v1/health, the Playwright install and all five acceptance identities each succeeded; the bootstrap then failed at scripts/dev/owner-acceptance/create-owner-account.mjs, because alignLocalJwtSigning recreates the GoTrue container (docker rm -f then docker run -d) and assertHs256 probed the token endpoint once with no retry — the recreate returned at 21:38:21.029 and the probe failed with 502 ten milliseconds later. A readiness race in the acceptance bootstrap, not the algorithm refusal its error text blamed, and not a limitation of hosted CI. ZERO tests executed; the zero-test guard failed the run rather than reporting green. (2) Run 31343632011, commit 0c40499be0a6a42dc984436437ffff9d90d45e5d, job 93321402511: FAILED, and this is the first time this tier ever produced test results anywhere but the Owner machine — 212 passed, 11 failed. The readiness race was gone (align-local-jwt.mjs now retries for 30 s on 502/503/504 and ECONNREFUSED only). The eleven were real product and test defects: seven isolation assertions that had begun measuring the loading skeleton rather than the rendered page, two planted accessibility violations, and two duplicate queues issuing no POST. (3) Run 31347643485, commit 78c458723671ac1c7d7c8721a09d4fd156283054, job 93332452247: PASSED. 229 tests planned, 225 passed, 0 failed, 224 executed across all 6 spec files in 3.2 minutes. The job conclusion is success. NOTE that the RUN conclusion is failure — other jobs in that workflow were red at that commit — which is exactly why this file, the gate and the workflow all read the per-job conclusion on the commit and never the run-level one. (4) Run 31508526699, commit 424e5d884ed7c8f608c446408743cbf88ac80515, job 93836261616: PASSED. 229 tests planned, 225 passed, 0 failed, 224 executed across all 6 spec files in 3.1 minutes. THIS IS THE CLOSING CANDIDATE. It is the run P1-27-QA-005 seals against, and it supersedes run 31347643485 as the evidence any current claim about this tier must cite — that run measured 78c4587, which is not the commit this phase closes on. WHAT IS AND IS NOT SETTLED. Settled: this tier runs on a hosted runner, and has passed there. SETTLED at the closing candidate by run (4): the tier has been observed to pass on the commit this phase closes on, with authenticated-browser sitting in the needs of both ci-gate and protected-gate. The earlier caveat on this field — that no run had been observed at the closing candidate — is discharged, and is kept here in the record rather than deleted, because it was true for three of the four runs above. Three fix waves changed 37 product files after 38afa5c28e5b78d484a442cf6b8596fb2a5c34aa, so P1-28-QA-005 re-froze its candidate at 6392ccb4321b004ed12e5d04ad583298da3303dd and every hosted figure taken from run 31750364479 is recorded there as PENDING at that candidate, marked `describesSupersededHead`, and listed in `pendingHostedBindings`. What it does not settle is the current candidate, and no run has yet been taken at it. Record that run here as (7), with its id, its commit and its counts, exactly as (1) through (6) were. policy: An entry in `unrun` is a debt, not a dispensation. It must name what the pull-request gate does not prove, why that job does not run it, which job does, what remains unrepaid, what compensates today, and a date by which the arrangement is revisited. tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts fails when a spec is neither executed by a gate-governed job nor declared here, when a declared spec IS executed by the pull-request gate (a declaration must not be able to hide a runnable tier), when a field is missing, when the named executing job does not exist in the workflow it names, and when reviewBy has passed. It also fails in the OTHER direction: while the tier is governed, an entry may not be re-added here — a debt must not outlive its repayment. `unrunNonBrowser` carries the same obligation in its own shape and is held to it by the same file. An entry must name the path, what it proves, what is unproven without it, why no hosted job runs it, THE COMMAND that does run it, why no local aggregate runs it either, what is still owed, what compensates, an owner and a review date. Every one of those is checked rather than read: the path must exist and must NOT be a browser spec, so the two registers cannot be confused for one another; the command must be a script this repository really declares; no workflow under .github/workflows may name either the command or the path, which is what turns "no hosted job runs it" from a sentence into a measurement; and no other package script may name the command, which does the same for "no local aggregate runs it". The forward direction binds here too: the day a hosted job or an aggregate picks the file up, those cases fail and the entry has to be deleted in that same change. Nothing in this register relaxes anything in the one above it — in particular the guard that refuses a declaration outside the gated browser directory is untouched, which is why this is a second register rather than a wider first one.
howToClose: CLOSED. Both steps of the recorded plan were carried out. The job was added to DECLARED_JOBS in scripts/ci/evaluate-ci-gate.mjs and to the `needs` of both `protected-gate` and `ci-gate`, which required the job to exist in pr-ci.yml as well — done by moving the body into a reusable workflow called from both — and therefore required the job counts in docs/engineering/ci-automation/pull-request-body.md to be updated in the same commit, which they were, derived from the workflows rather than typed. A passing hosted execution HAS since been observed — run 31347643485, job 93332452247, 225 passed and 0 failed. See `hostedObservation` for all six runs, one by one. What is still owed is not an execution but an execution AT THE CLOSING CANDIDATE: every observed run predates the merge of the five remediation branches, and QA-005 is the measurement that seals the tier against the final head. Governing the check before it had ever gone green was the correct order, and it remains correct now for a different reason — the gate refuses a merge whose candidate this tier has not been run against.

governed.since: 415a869d72141cbab5ee2079cdae695e232ecdc9 — the commit that added .github/workflows/_reusable-authenticated-browser.yml and put the job in both gates. Named as a sha because every sibling field names a checkable artefact and a description is not one: a reader could not verify the previous wording without first reconstructing the search it describes.
governed.executedBy: .github/workflows/_reusable-authenticated-browser.yml job `authenticated-browser`, called by `pr-ci.yml` (same-repository pull requests only) and by `protected-develop-verification.yml` (every push to develop and main, and before a merge by workflow_dispatch pinned to a candidate-sha).
governed.governedBy: `ci-gate` in pr-ci.yml and `protected-gate` in protected-develop-verification.yml. Both list `authenticated-browser` in `needs`; `scripts/ci/evaluate-ci-gate.mjs` declares it `alwaysRequired` and refuses to accept a skip of it unless the caller states `--trusted-context false`, in which case the state is reported as `NOT_ELIGIBLE_FOR_SECURITY_REASON` and never as a pass.
governed.forkPolicy: A pull request from a fork does NOT receive this job: it stands a full Supabase stack, a production API and a real operator account up on the runner, and untrusted code must not be given privileged execution. The gate is told so explicitly and records the refusal; it does not infer it from the absence of a result.
governed.p1-31-acceptance-specs: The last FIVE paths are the P1-31 QA-005 acceptance specs. Four were added by feature/p1-31-acceptance-harness; overview-p1-31.spec.ts was added by feature/p1-31-acceptance-rerun, which is also what rewrote the other four. They are on THIS list and not in `unrun` because the fact decided it and not the convenience: `apps/web/playwright.config.ts:204` and `:215` give the `authenticated-en` and `authenticated-ar` projects `testMatch: /authenticated[\\/].*\.spec\.ts/`, a directory-wide glob that matches them the moment they exist, and `.github/workflows/_reusable-authenticated-browser.yml:416` sets `ROOTLCO_E2E_AUTH: '1'` and runs `npm run test:web-e2e-authenticated`. So the governed job DOES execute them. Two of this file's own rules independently forbid the other answer: `policy` fails a declaration whose spec IS executed by the gate, and the last case in tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts fails any `/authenticated/` entry in `unrun` while the tier is governed. `authenticated-tablet` MATCHES THEM TOO, since the widening recorded at the end of `hostedObservation`: its `testMatch` at `:255-256` now names `(administration|appointments-and-receptions|audit-log-p1-31|delivery-p1-31|delivery-writes-p1-31|overview-p1-31|reports-p1-31|warranty-p1-31)`, so the six run at 1024x768 as well, for the reason `docs/phase-1/phase-1-31/canonical-plan.md:220-226` gives — the one description the chapter applies to all sixteen Frontend tasks names desktop/tablet among the obligations binding every one of them. The previous wording here said the opposite and was true when it was written; it is corrected rather than kept, because it is a statement about the tree as it stands and not a record of a run. WHAT THEY DO WHEN EXECUTED, stated so that no reader mistakes registration for coverage. EACH of the five files carries at least one case that runs on THIS job's environment and asserts what it provides, because a spec file that executes nothing here is a file nobody would notice breaking - and the `A run that collected nothing is a failure, not a pass` step below fails PER FILE for exactly that reason. The environment is read from this workflow rather than assumed: `npm run supabase:reset` applies every migration and seed, `npm run acceptance:create-owner` creates Tenant A, Tenant B and the acceptance owner, both applications are built and served, and `auth.setup.ts` signs in through the product's own login form. The owner's permission set is `OWNER_PERMISSIONS` in scripts/dev/owner-acceptance/context.mjs. It is described by MEMBERSHIP and never by a count: it is a runtime union of four sets, so a number written here would be a second statement of something no contract owns, and the figure `60` recorded here previously was already prose rather than an assertion. It HOLDS `sal.delivery.view`, `wo.work_order.read`, `sal.finance.view`, `wty.warranty.read`, `iam.audit.view`, `org.company.read` and `org.branch.read`; it does NOT hold `rpt.report.read` or `wty.policy.manage`. The earlier wording here named `wty.warranty.manage`, which is not the code the plan-creation panel gates on and is not a code any P1-31 screen consults; `wty.policy.manage` is. Both directions of that membership are now asserted mechanically by tests/ci/p1-31-account-manifest.test.ts against the two permission authorities, and the same two sets are published to the browser tier as apps/web/tests/e2e/authenticated/account-manifest.json. That set is P1-28-shaped and was not widened for this phase, so the asymmetry is a fact about the environment and not a choice. The unconditional cases assert ONE PINNED OUTCOME PER CREDENTIAL KIND, derived from that manifest rather than read off the page: the delivery queue's three-code conjunction passes and the screen states the idle reason its directory access entails; both warranty reads render while the plan-create panel is withheld from the same session; the report catalogue, the report run screen and the operational overview each render the whole refusal this account is owed and leak no part of the surface behind the gate; and the audit log renders its no-export statement, which never needed journey data at all. The previous 'either the surface or a complete refusal' shape is gone from all five files: a case that passes whichever way the screen answers cannot fail for the reason it exists. WHAT STILL SKIPS is every case that asserts on a record the journey made - a specific delivery id, a generated warranty, a report's row count, an overview section's summary - because `ROOTLCO_P131_HANDOFF` is unset here and the harness has never been run. Those cases now carry a SECOND gate as well: they run only when the browser is signed in as the very organisation administrator whose records they are about, decided by auth.setup.ts from the address it signed in with and written to account-kind.json beside the storage state. Each of those skips states its own reason in the run output; the shared text is `NO_HANDOFF_REASON` in apps/web/tests/e2e/authenticated/p1-31-handoff.ts. The division is the rule: behind the handoff if and only if it needs journey data. Nothing in this entry, and nothing in the specs, weakens the zero-executed-test step, exempts the directory or adds a suppression - the step is satisfied because every file now really does execute. Recorded in docs/phase-1/phase-1-31/acceptance-plan.md sections 3 and 3.0, which list all five specs and what each asserts without a handoff, and section 8.1, which carries the three overview cases and states the account-kind gating; and in the register section this lane appends at its merge-queue turn. Section 52 of the phase change-control is NOT cited as the record of these five: it predates this lane and its 'resolved by relocation' disposition is withdrawn at that same turn.

unrunNonBrowser.whatItProves: That the privileged export-fixture writer really works against a real PostgreSQL: every statement it issues, its transaction boundaries, its confirmation token, its attempt bound, its four freshness predicates, its advisory-lock lease, its exclusive evidence reservation, its audit append with the hash chain, its three deferred constraint triggers, and the permission lookup it performs on a connection holding neither SUPERUSER nor BYPASSRLS.
unrunNonBrowser.whatIsUnprovenWithoutIt: Without it the only evidence for that writer is tests/ci/p1-31-export-fixture-refusals.test.ts, which drives the whole refusal matrix with no database at all. That file proves the guards and proves nothing whatever about the SQL underneath them, and a deferred constraint in particular cannot be observed by anything that never opens a transaction. So a green pull request leaves the statements themselves unexecuted, and the grant path that installs a scoped expiring role is asserted rather than run.
unrunNonBrowser.whyNoHostedJobRunsIt: It needs a DISPOSABLE database, and no hosted job has one to give it. The file refuses to run when current_database() is the shared acceptance name, because it installs privileged grants and writing those into the shared environment would contaminate a run in progress; every hosted database job supplies exactly that shared name at job level. The two are incompatible by construction, and the alternative — relaxing the refusal into a skip so the file could ride the shared tier — would put a privileged writer one environment variable away from the acceptance database and report the near miss as green.
unrunNonBrowser.executedByCommand: npm run test:db-fixture, with DB_NAME pointing at a disposable database built by scripts/db/apply-migrations.mjs plus the seven files of supabase/seeds/ in numeric order. NO hosted job runs this command and no local aggregate runs it either; it is an explicit operator proof, classified `environment` in scripts/ci/check-command-coverage.mjs, and the closing acceptance procedure names both the command and the database so that it is taken deliberately rather than assumed.
unrunNonBrowser.whyNoLocalAggregateRunsIt: vitest.config.db.ts excludes the file by name, so `npm run test:db` and `npm run test:backend` do not collect it, and it is not a unit-tier file so `npm run test:unit` never saw it. Its own configuration, vitest.config.db-fixture.ts, includes that one path and is reached only by the command above, which sits in no aggregate script.
unrunNonBrowser.remainingDebt: An execution of this command at the closing candidate, recorded with the head and the database it ran against. It is owed as an operator proof and not as a gate result: this entry sits in the `needs` of no gate and cannot, because neither `ci-gate` nor `protected-gate` can wait on a job that does not exist. Until a disposable database can be stood up on a runner, the debt is discharged by the recorded run and never by a check mark.
unrunNonBrowser.compensatingControl: tests/ci/p1-31-export-fixture-refusals.test.ts runs on the pull-request gate and drives the whole refusal matrix without a database, so every guard, every precondition and every refusal path is exercised there even though the SQL is not. The loopback guard is covered only by that file, because it is the one thing the database-backed file substitutes.
